angle: Base-task SOTA deep learning models for encrypted network traffic classification (the models XAI work explains)
sources_used: Semantic Scholar Graph API (search + batch, via curl)

papers.title: Malware traffic classification using convolutional neural network for representation learning
papers.authors: Wei Wang, Ming Zhu, Xuewen Zeng, Xiaozhou Ye, Yiqiang Sheng
papers.input_representation: raw session bytes rendered as 28x28 grayscale image
papers.relevance: First representation-learning traffic classifier: raw session bytes are rendered as a grayscale image and fed to a 2D-CNN (introduced USTC-TFC2016); saliency on these byte-images is the archetypal explanation target.

papers.title: End-to-end encrypted traffic classification with one-dimensional convolution neural networks
papers.authors: Wei Wang, Ming Zhu, Jinlin Wang, Xuewen Zeng, Zhongzhen Yang
papers.input_representation: first 784 raw bytes of a session/flow (1D vector)
papers.relevance: Canonical 1D-CNN on the first 784 raw bytes of a session, end-to-end on ISCX VPN-nonVPN; the default raw-byte baseline nearly every XAI-for-traffic paper explains or attacks.

papers.title: Deep packet: a novel approach for encrypted traffic classification using deep learning
papers.authors: Mohammad Lotfollahi, Mahdi Jafari Siavoshani, Ramin Shirali Hossein Zade, Mohammdsadegh Saberian
papers.input_representation: first 1500 raw IP-packet bytes (masked MAC/IP), 1D vector
papers.relevance: Deep Packet: stacked autoencoder + 1D-CNN over the first 1500 raw packet bytes (identifying header fields masked to avoid bias) for app identification and traffic characterization on ISCX; the single most-cited raw-byte model that XAI studies explain.

papers.title: Datanet: Deep Learning Based Encrypted Network Traffic Classification in SDN Home Gateway
papers.authors: Pan Wang, Feng Ye, Xuejiao Chen, Yi Qian
papers.input_representation: raw packet bytes (per-packet vectors)
papers.relevance: Datanet trains MLP, stacked-autoencoder, and CNN classifiers on raw packet bytes of ISCX VPN-nonVPN for app-aware SDN home-gateway control; a canonical multi-architecture raw-byte baseline.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Encrypted Traffic Classification: An Overview
papers.input_representation: survey: taxonomy of raw bytes / time-series / header fields / flow statistics inputs
papers.relevance: The standard early survey that fixed the taxonomy of input representations (raw bytes, packet time-series, header fields, flow statistics) and the general DL framework the XAI literature assumes.

papers.title: FS-Net: A Flow Sequence Network For Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.authors: Chang Liu, Longtao He, Gang Xiong, Zigang Cao, Zhen Li
papers.input_representation: packet-length sequence of a flow (no payload)
papers.relevance: FS-Net: multi-layer bi-GRU encoder-decoder with reconstruction loss over raw packet-length sequences only; the canonical sequence-model baseline whose explanations live in packet-size/timing space rather than byte space.

papers.title: FlowPic: A Generic Representation for Encrypted Traffic Classification and Applications Identification
papers.input_representation: 2D histogram image of packet sizes vs. arrival times per flow window
papers.relevance: FlowPic turns a flow into a 2D packet-size/arrival-time histogram image classified by a LeNet-style CNN (VPN and Tor categories); pixel-saliency explanations map back to size-time bins, making it a favorite XAI subject.

papers.title: MIMETIC: Mobile encrypted traffic classification using multimodal deep learning
papers.authors: Giuseppe Aceto, Domenico Ciuonzo, Antonio Montieri, Antonio Pescape
papers.input_representation: multimodal: first payload bytes + per-packet protocol-field sequence (dir/size/TCP win/IAT)
papers.relevance: MIMETIC fuses two modalities - raw payload bytes and packet-level protocol-field sequences - with intra/inter-modality learning for mobile app classification; multimodal inputs mean explanations must attribute across heterogeneous views.

papers.title: Mobile Encrypted Traffic Classification Using Deep Learning: Experimental Evaluation, Lessons Learned, and Challenges
papers.authors: Giuseppe Aceto, Domenico Ciuonzo, Antonio Montieri, Antonio Pescape
papers.input_representation: systematic comparison: payload bytes vs. protocol-field time series inputs
papers.relevance: The reference experimental evaluation of SAE/CNN/LSTM mobile traffic classifiers across input designs (payload bytes vs. header-field series), explicitly cataloguing dataset/input pitfalls - groundwork every explanation study cites.

papers.title: Lucid: A Practical, Lightweight Deep Learning Solution for DDoS Attack Detection
papers.authors: R. Doriguzzi-Corin, S. Millar, S. Scott-Hayward, J. Martinez-del-Rincon, D. Siracusa
papers.input_representation: per-flow matrix of 11 packet-level attributes x n packets (packet-feature sequence)
papers.relevance: LUCID: lightweight CNN over a flow matrix of 11 per-packet attributes for DDoS detection with 40x faster inference; its authors also published a companion activation-analysis, making it a standard explainability testbed for attack detection.

papers.title: DeepMAL - Deep Learning Models for Malware Traffic Detection and Classification
papers.authors: Gonzalo Marin, Pedro Casas, German Capdehourat
papers.input_representation: raw bytestream at packet level and flow level (first bytes, no handcrafted features)
papers.relevance: DeepMAL: LSTM+1D-CNN on raw byte streams at both packet and flow granularity for malware traffic (Stratosphere IPS captures), showing raw-flow input (98.6%) beats raw-packet (77.6%) - a clean case study in how input granularity changes what needs explaining.

papers.title: New Directions in Automated Traffic Analysis (nPrint / nPrintML)
papers.authors: Jordan Holland, Paul Schmitt, Nick Feamster, Prateek Mittal
papers.input_representation: nPrint: constant-size bit-aligned binary packet representation (every header bit a feature, -1 padding)
papers.relevance: nPrint defines a standard bit-level packet representation consumed by AutoML (nPrintML); because each input bit maps to a named protocol header bit, feature-importance explanations are directly semantically interpretable - the paper itself does such model analysis.

papers.title: PERT: Payload Encoding Representation from Transformer for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.authors: Hong Ye He, Zhi Guo Yang, Xiang Ning Chen
papers.input_representation: payload bytes tokenized as words for BERT-style dynamic word embedding
papers.relevance: PERT is the first BERT-style pre-training applied to encrypted traffic: payload bytes are tokenized and contextually embedded, then fine-tuned for classification; starts the pre-trained-transformer line whose attention maps XAI work probes.

papers.title: Accurate Decentralized Application Identification via Encrypted Traffic Analysis Using Graph Neural Networks (GraphDApp)
papers.authors: Meng Shen, Jinpeng Zhang, Liehuang Zhu, Ke Xu, Xiaojiang Du
papers.input_representation: Traffic Interaction Graph (TIG) built from packet sizes/directions of bidirectional bursts
papers.relevance: GraphDApp converts a flow's bidirectional packet-size interactions into a Traffic Interaction Graph classified by a GNN for DApp fingerprinting (1,300 DApps); graph inputs invite subgraph-style (GNNExplainer-like) explanations, unlike byte saliency.

papers.title: CGNN: Traffic Classification with Graph Neural Network
papers.authors: Bo Pang, Yongquan Fu, Siyuan Ren, Ye Wang, Qing Liao, Yan Jia
papers.input_representation: chained graph over the packet stream (packets as nodes, sequential edges)
papers.relevance: CGNN builds a chained graph over the packet stream and applies a graph classifier for app/malicious/encrypted traffic, arguing packet compositional structure is lost by CNN/RNN models - another graph input representation for explanation methods.

papers.title: TSCRNN: A novel classification scheme of encrypted traffic based on flow spatiotemporal features for efficient management of IIoT
papers.authors: Kunda Lin, Xiaolong Xu, Honghao Gao
papers.input_representation: raw byte segments of flows: CNN spatial features + stacked BiLSTM temporal features
papers.relevance: TSCRNN extracts spatial features from raw flow bytes with CNN then temporal dependencies with stacked BiLSTM for IIoT encrypted traffic; a widely-cited CNN+RNN hybrid baseline in later XAI comparisons.

papers.title: ET-BERT: A Contextualized Datagram Representation with Pre-training Transformers for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.authors: Xinjie Lin, Gang Xiong, Gaopeng Gou, Zhen Li, Junzheng Shi, Jing Yu
papers.input_representation: raw datagram bytes tokenized as hex 'BURST' token sequences (BPE over byte pairs)
papers.relevance: ET-BERT pre-trains a BERT encoder on raw-byte BURST tokens with masked-BURST and same-origin-BURST tasks, then fine-tunes per packet or flow (SOTA on ISCX, CSTNET-TLS 1.3); it is THE reference pre-trained model that current XAI-for-traffic papers try to explain.

papers.title: Rosetta: Enabling Robust TLS Encrypted Traffic Classification in Diverse Network Environments with TCP-Aware Traffic Augmentation
papers.authors: Renjie Xie, Jiahao Cao, Enhuan Dong, Mingwei Xu, Kun Sun, Qi Li, Licheng Shen, Menghao Zhang
papers.input_representation: packet-length sequences of TLS flows, made invariant via TCP-aware augmentation + self-supervised features
papers.relevance: Rosetta shows existing DL classifiers 'all have significant performance degradation in real diverse network environments' because TCP mechanics reshape packet-length sequences, and fixes it with TCP-aware augmentation; key evidence that learned features are fragile artifacts - central to XAI motivation.

papers.title: Yet Another Traffic Classifier: A Masked Autoencoder Based Traffic Transformer with Multi-Level Flow Representation (YaTC)
papers.authors: Ruijie Zhao, Mingwei Zhan, Xianwen Deng, Yanhao Wang, Yijun Wang, Guan Gui, Zhi Xue
papers.input_representation: Multi-level Flow Representation (MFR) matrix: header+payload bytes of first packets formatted as a single-channel image
papers.relevance: YaTC pre-trains a masked-autoencoder traffic transformer over an MFR byte-image with packet-level and flow-level attention, fine-tuned with few labels (SOTA on 5 datasets); with MIETT/NetMamba it defines the MAE family whose patch attributions XAI work visualizes.

papers.title: A Novel Self-Supervised Framework Based on Masked Autoencoder for Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: byte matrix (MFR-style) with masked-autoencoder self-supervision
papers.relevance: Journal extension of the YaTC line: MAE self-supervised pre-training over formatted byte matrices for traffic classification, consolidating the masked-reconstruction paradigm on traffic bytes.

papers.title: TFE-GNN: A Temporal Fusion Encoder Using Graph Neural Networks for Fine-grained Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.authors: Haozhen Zhang, Le Yu, Xi Xiao, Qing Li, Francesco Mercaldo, Xiapu Luo, Qixu Liu
papers.input_representation: byte-level graphs per packet (bytes as nodes, PMI co-occurrence edges), separate header/payload graphs
papers.relevance: TFE-GNN encodes each packet's raw bytes as a point-wise-mutual-information graph, embeds header and payload graphs with dual GNNs and cross-gated fusion, then fuses temporally; the canonical byte-graph model, where explanations become node/edge importance over bytes.

papers.title: MTC: A Multi-Task Model for Encrypted Network Traffic Classification Based on Transformer and 1D-CNN
papers.authors: Kunda Wang, Jia Gao, Xiaoqin Lei
papers.input_representation: raw session bytes fed in parallel to Transformer (long-range) and 1D-CNN (local) branches
papers.relevance: MTC fuses parallel Transformer and 1D-CNN branches over raw bytes for joint app identification and traffic characterization on ISCX VPN-nonVPN (F1 ~98%); a representative hybrid-architecture explained in multi-task XAI settings.

papers.title: AutoML4ETC: Automated Neural Architecture Search for Real-World Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: first packet-header bytes of a flow (early classification)
papers.relevance: AutoML4ETC searches neural architectures over early packet-header-byte inputs, beating hand-designed classifiers on real orange-telecom and QUIC traffic; shows the architecture itself is a searchable hyperparameter, complicating model-specific explanations.

papers.title: NetGPT: Generative Pretrained Transformer for Network Traffic
papers.authors: Xuying Meng, Chungang Lin, Yequan Wang, Yujun Zhang
papers.input_representation: hex-encoded header+payload tokens as unified text; field shuffling and prompts
papers.relevance: NetGPT is the first generative (GPT-style) pretrained traffic model supporting both understanding and generation, encoding raw traffic as hex text with header-field shuffling for task adaptation - the generative branch of traffic foundation models.

papers.title: netFound: Foundation Model for Network Security (Principled Design for Network Foundation Models)
papers.authors: Satyandra Guthula, Roman Beltiukov, Navya Battula, Wenbo Guo, Arpit Gupta
papers.input_representation: protocol-aware tokenized packet headers + flow metadata (IATs, bytes) with burst-flow hierarchical attention; privacy-by-construction (payload-light)
papers.relevance: netFound pre-trains a hierarchical burst-flow transformer with protocol-aware tokenization on a billion-token telemetry corpus (weights and pipeline released); its 'principled design' axes - tokenization, hierarchy, context embedding - define what a faithful explanation of a traffic FM must respect.

papers.title: Lens: A Knowledge-Guided Foundation Model for Network Traffic
papers.input_representation: raw traffic as text: plain-text header fields + encrypted payload bytes, T5 encoder-decoder
papers.relevance: Lens is a T5-based traffic foundation model whose knowledge-guided pretraining mixes plain-text protocol headers with encrypted payload bytes across understanding and generation tasks - representative of the encoder-decoder FM branch.

papers.title: TrafficGPT: Breaking the Token Barrier for Efficient Long Traffic Analysis and Generation
papers.input_representation: long byte-token sequences (~12k tokens) with linear attention over flows
papers.relevance: TrafficGPT extends generative traffic pre-training to ~12k-token flows via linear attention, jointly serving classification and generation; addresses the token-length ceiling that truncates most byte-input models (a hidden input-representation bias XAI should surface).

papers.title: NetMamba: Efficient Network Traffic Classification via Pre-training Unidirectional Mamba
papers.authors: Tongze Wang, Xiaohui Xie, Wenduo Wang, Chuyi Wang, Youjian Zhao, Yong Cui
papers.input_representation: byte-level multimodal flow representation (MFR-style byte matrix), unidirectional state-space model
papers.relevance: NetMamba swaps the transformer for a unidirectional Mamba SSM pre-trained MAE-style on byte-level flow representations, matching accuracy at much lower latency; SSMs lack attention maps entirely, which changes what explanation tooling can use.

papers.title: TrafficFormer: An Efficient Pre-trained Model for Traffic Data
papers.input_representation: raw-byte field tokens; fine-grained multi-classification pretext + random-initialization field augmentation
papers.relevance: TrafficFormer (S&P'25) strengthens ET-BERT-style pre-training with a fine-grained flow-similarity pretext task and field-randomizing augmentation to 'focus on key information' - the current top venue-validated pre-trained ETC model and a prime explanation target.

papers.title: MIETT: Multi-Instance Encrypted Traffic Transformer for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: flow as bag of packets; hex byte tokens with two-level (token-level + packet-level) attention
papers.relevance: MIETT treats a flow as a multi-instance bag of packets with dual-level attention and packet-order/contrastive pre-training tasks, capturing both token and packet relationships - the two-level attention structure is exactly what attention-based explanations need to respect.

papers.title: Revolutionizing Encrypted Traffic Classification with MH-Net: A Multi-View Heterogeneous Graph Model
papers.input_representation: multi-view heterogeneous traffic graphs: bits aggregated into traffic units at multiple granularities
papers.relevance: MH-Net (TFE-GNN successors) aggregates different numbers of bits into 'traffic units' forming multi-view heterogeneous graphs trained with contrastive multi-task learning; state of the art of the graph-input family.

papers.title: One Train for Two Tasks: An Encrypted Traffic Classification Framework Using Supervised Contrastive Learning (CLE-TFE)
papers.input_representation: byte-level traffic graphs with graph augmentation; joint packet-level and flow-level tasks
papers.relevance: Applies supervised contrastive learning and graph augmentation on byte-level traffic graphs, classifying packet and flow levels in one training run; representative of contrastive refinements to the byte-graph representation.

papers.title: TrafficLLM: Enhancing Large Language Models for Network Traffic Analysis with Generic Traffic Representation
papers.input_representation: traffic-domain tokenization of raw traffic + natural-language instructions (dual-stage LLM fine-tuning)
papers.relevance: TrafficLLM adapts general LLMs to traffic via traffic-domain tokenization and dual-stage instruction/representation tuning with parameter-efficient adaptation, generalizing across detection and generation tasks - the LLM-adaptation branch of the base-model landscape.

papers.title: MERLOT: A Distilled LLM-based Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Scalable Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: contextual feature embeddings of traffic fed to distilled GPT-2 expert models (MoE)
papers.relevance: MERLOT distills GPT-2-based experts into a mixture-of-experts encrypted-traffic classifier for deployment-scale inference; MoE routing adds another layer (which expert fired and why) that explanations must cover.

papers.title: MM4flow: A Pre-trained Multi-modal Model for Versatile Network Traffic Analysis
papers.input_representation: multi-modal: byte content + flow-level modalities pre-trained jointly
papers.relevance: MM4flow (CCS'25) is a pre-trained multi-modal traffic model unifying content and flow modalities for versatile downstream analysis - the newest top-venue entry in the traffic foundation-model line.

papers.title: FlowletFormer: Network Behavioral Semantic Aware Pre-training Model for Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: protocol-stack-aligned tokenization of packet sequences and flowlets
papers.relevance: FlowletFormer argues generic BERT tokenization ignores network behavioral semantics and aligns tokens/segments with the protocol stack and flowlet structure - directly about making the input representation semantically meaningful (hence explainable).

papers.title: TraGe: A Generic Packet Representation for Traffic Classification Based on Header-Payload Differences
papers.input_representation: packet bytes with differentiated header vs. payload masking during pre-training
papers.relevance: TraGe pre-trains with header/payload-differentiated masking, exploiting the fact that header bytes and encrypted payload bytes have fundamentally different statistics - the header-payload heterogeneity theme recurring across 2025-2026 models.

papers.title: Nethira: A Heterogeneity-aware Hierarchical Pre-trained Model for Network Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: hierarchical byte / protocol-field / packet-level reconstruction over raw sequences
papers.relevance: Nethira (2026) pre-trains with hierarchical reconstruction spanning byte, protocol, and packet levels of raw traffic - the current frontier of heterogeneity-aware traffic pre-training.

papers.title: MambaNetBurst: Direct Byte-level Network Traffic Classification without Tokenization or Pretraining
papers.input_representation: fixed-length raw-byte bursts from the first few packets, Mamba-2 backbone, no tokenizer
papers.relevance: MambaNetBurst classifies fixed-length raw-byte bursts with a Mamba-2 backbone and no tokenization or pre-training, challenging the assumption that traffic needs BERT-style pipelines at all - a counterpoint model for explanation studies.

papers.title: Fine-grained TLS Services Classification with Reject Option
papers.input_representation: packet metadata sequences (sizes, directions, IATs) + flow statistics; CESNET-TLS22 ISP-scale dataset
papers.relevance: Introduces the ISP-scale CESNET-TLS22 dataset (140M+ flows, 191 services) and a 1D-CNN over packet-metadata sequences with an unknown-class reject option; the production-realistic base model and dataset increasingly used to sanity-check lab results.

papers.title: Universal Embedding Function for Traffic Classification via QUIC Domain Recognition Pretraining: A Transfer Learning Success
papers.input_representation: packet-sequence features of QUIC flows; embedding pre-trained with ArcFace on SNI-domain recognition
papers.relevance: Pre-trains a universal flow-embedding by recognizing QUIC SNI domains with metric learning, then transfers to classification tasks - a non-byte, metadata-sequence route to traffic foundation embeddings.

papers.title: Replication: Contrastive Learning and Data Augmentation in Traffic Classification Using a Flowpic Input Representation
papers.input_representation: flowpic (packet-size/time histogram image) with contrastive augmentation
papers.relevance: Replicates a UCDavis flowpic contrastive-learning result, uncovering dataset problems and smaller-than-reported gains; a rare reproducibility audit of a base representation - evidence for why explanation/validation tooling is needed.

papers.title: Data Augmentation for Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: packet time-series / flowpic inputs under systematic augmentation study
papers.relevance: Systematically benchmarks augmentation strategies for traffic-classification inputs, showing which invariances actually hold for packet series - defines the perturbation space that perturbation-based XAI methods implicitly assume.

papers.title: Many or Few Samples? Comparing Transfer, Contrastive and Meta-Learning in Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: packet-series and payload inputs under transfer/contrastive/meta-learning regimes
papers.relevance: Head-to-head comparison of transfer, meta-, and contrastive learning for label-scarce ETC, finding contrastive representation reuse most effective - maps the label-efficiency axis along which pre-trained base models are chosen.

papers.title: A Lightweight, Efficient and Explainable-by-Design Convolutional Neural Network for Internet Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: packet-level input series designed so each convolution maps to interpretable traffic concepts
papers.relevance: The bridge paper: a CNN traffic classifier explicitly architected to be explainable-by-design (deployed at a large ISP), demonstrating the alternative to post-hoc XAI over opaque byte models.

papers.title: The Sweet Danger of Sugar: Debunking Representation Learning for Encrypted Traffic Classification (Pcap-Encoder)
papers.input_representation: critique of raw-byte inputs; proposes Pcap-Encoder, an LM that extracts features from protocol headers only
papers.relevance: Debunks byte-level representation-learning ETC: shows benchmark artifacts (header leftovers) rather than payload semantics drive reported accuracy, and that a header-focused LM (Pcap-Encoder) suffices - the strongest published statement of the shortcut-learning problem XAI-for-traffic must detect.

papers.title: Bias in the Shadows: Explore Shortcuts in Encrypted Network Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: model-agnostic audit of statistical shortcuts in raw binary traffic inputs
papers.relevance: A model-agnostic framework that hunts shortcut features (spurious statistical correlations in raw bytes) exploited by ETC models across datasets - the empirical companion to Sweet-Danger and the direct problem statement for explanation-based auditing.

papers.title: Demystifying Network Foundation Models
papers.input_representation: probing/analysis of latent spaces of byte-token network foundation models
papers.relevance: Analyzes what network foundation models (ET-BERT/YaTC/netFound-class) actually encode in their latent spaces via probing - the first interpretability-flavored anatomy of traffic FMs and a hinge between the base-model and XAI literatures.

papers.title: NetBench: A Large-Scale and Comprehensive Network Traffic Benchmark Dataset for Foundation Models
papers.input_representation: benchmark suite over packet/flow byte inputs, 20 tasks
papers.relevance: Benchmark unifying 20 classification/generation tasks for traffic foundation models; the shared yardstick on which the 2024-2026 base models report.

papers.title: UniAlign: A Model-Agnostic Framework for Robust Network Traffic Classification under Distribution Shifts
papers.input_representation: model-agnostic alignment layer over existing classifiers' representations
papers.relevance: Model-agnostic robustness wrapper aligning representations of existing traffic classifiers under distribution shift - part of the robustness wave (with Rosetta, FG-SAT) responding to fragile learned features.

papers.title: FG-SAT: Efficient Flow Graph for Encrypted Traffic Classification under Environment Shifts
papers.input_representation: flow graph of internal flow relationships; feature selection via Jensen-Shannon divergence
papers.relevance: Represents flows as graphs of internal relationships with divergence-based feature selection to survive environment shifts - graph-input robustness work motivated by the same deployment fragility XAI aims to diagnose.

papers.title: Facing Unknown: Open-World Encrypted Traffic Classification Based on Contrastive Pre-Training
papers.input_representation: contrastive pre-training over flows; GAN-synthesized marginal flows for unknown detection
papers.relevance: Open-world ETC via contrastive pre-training plus GAN-based marginal-flow synthesis to detect unknown classes; represents the open-set assumption-relaxation that closed-world base models (and their explanations) usually ignore.

papers.title: Deep Fingerprinting: Undermining Website Fingerprinting Defenses with Deep Learning
papers.authors: Payap Sirinam, Mohsen Imani, Marc Juarez, Matthew Wright
papers.input_representation: packet direction sequence (+-1 vector, length 5000) of Tor traffic
papers.relevance: Deep Fingerprinting: CNN over packet-direction sequences that broke WTF-PAD (98% on Tor); the sibling task (website fingerprinting) whose XAI treatments are frequently cross-cited by traffic-classification explanation work.

papers.title: TrafficGPT: An LLM Approach for Open-Set Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: LLM over traffic tokens for open-set recognition
papers.relevance: LLM-based open-set encrypted traffic classification (distinct from the 2403.05822 TrafficGPT), showing the LLM branch also tackles unknown-class detection.

papers.title: SHAPE: A Simultaneous Header and Payload Encoding Model for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: separate header and payload byte encodings fused simultaneously
papers.relevance: Encodes header and payload bytes as separate views fused for classification under limited labels - early articulation of the header/payload heterogeneity now standard in 2025-2026 pre-trained models.

papers.title: PERO: Efficient Robust Post-Training Foundation Models for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: post-training of byte-sequence traffic foundation models with sample-wise risk proxy
papers.relevance: PERO post-trains encrypted-traffic foundation models for robustness using a lightweight sample-risk proxy - 2026 evidence that FM fragility is now treated as a first-class problem.

papers.title: Traffic-CBM: A Structurally Interpretable Multimodal Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: concept-bottleneck over flow statistics + packet sequences + byte-level views
papers.relevance: Concept-bottleneck traffic classifier organizing flow-stat, packet-sequence, and byte representations into a hierarchical concept space - interpretable-by-design counterweight to post-hoc XAI over byte transformers, sitting exactly on this corpus's boundary.

papers.title: Where Do Flow Semantics Reside? A Protocol-Native Tabular Pretraining Paradigm for Encrypted Traffic Classification (FlowSem-MAE)
papers.input_representation: tabular masked autoencoder over protocol-defined field units (Flow Semantic Units), not raw byte streams
papers.relevance: Asks the representation question head-on ('where do flow semantics reside?') and pre-trains a tabular MAE over protocol-defined field units instead of undifferentiated bytes - protocol-native inputs make attributions land on named fields.

papers.title: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Encrypted Traffic Classification on Resource-Constrained Devices
papers.input_representation: 1D-CNN over raw bytes (ISCX VPN-nonVPN) under memory/compute constraints
papers.relevance: HW-NAS compresses 1D-CNN raw-byte classifiers to IoT budgets on ISCX VPN-nonVPN; the tinyML end of the base-model spectrum where explanation cost also matters.

papers.title: One task to rule them all: A closer look at traffic classification generalizability
papers.input_representation: cross-task/cross-dataset evaluation of standard input representations
papers.relevance: Empirically tests whether traffic classifiers generalize across tasks and datasets (largely: they do not), quantifying the external-validity gap that shortcut-hunting explanations try to localize.

papers.title: Non-uniformity is All You Need: Efficient and Timely Encrypted Traffic Classification With ECHO
papers.input_representation: non-uniform bins of packet sizes and inter-arrival times; early-classification cascade
papers.relevance: ECHO optimizes non-uniform packet-size/timing binning plus an early-classification cascade - shows the size/time input representation itself is tunable, which changes attribution granularity.

papers.title: Generic Multi-modal Representation Learning for Network Traffic Analysis
papers.input_representation: multi-modal autoencoder over packet series + payload + flow statistics
papers.relevance: Generic multi-modal representation-learning framework spanning packet series, payload, and flow statistics for multiple traffic-analysis tasks - the modality-fusion direction MIMETIC started, in modern self-supervised form.

papers.title: PacketCLIP: Multi-Modal Embedding of Network Traffic and Language for Cybersecurity Reasoning
papers.input_representation: CLIP-style contrastive alignment of packet byte embeddings with natural-language descriptions; hierarchical GNN reasoning
papers.relevance: PacketCLIP contrastively aligns packet content with natural-language semantics for intrusion reasoning - traffic-to-language alignment is a nascent route to natural-language explanations of traffic models.

papers.title: NetMamba+: A Framework of Pre-trained Models for Efficient and Accurate Network Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: multimodal byte-preserving traffic representation over Mamba backbone
papers.relevance: NetMamba+ extends the Mamba pre-trained-classifier line with a multimodal byte-preserving representation - current frontier of the efficiency-oriented SSM family.

papers.title: TrafficMoE: Heterogeneity-aware Mixture of Experts for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.input_representation: disentangled header and payload streams routed to sparse experts with uncertainty-aware filtering
papers.relevance: TrafficMoE routes disentangled header vs. payload representations through sparse experts - the MoE + header/payload-heterogeneity synthesis closing out the 2026 model wave.

notes.recurring_datasets: ISCX VPN-nonVPN 2016 is near-universal (Deep Packet, Wang 1D/2D-CNN, Datanet, MTC, HW-NAS, ET-BERT...); also ISCX Tor 2016, USTC-TFC2016 (introduced by Wang ICOIN 2017), CIC-IDS2017/CSE-CIC-IDS2018 (Lucid), CSTNET-TLS 1.3 (introduced by ET-BERT), Cross-Platform Android/iOS (YaTC, TFE-GNN), CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020, UCDAVIS-19 QUIC (Flowpic replication), Mirage-19/22 (Aceto group), AppClassNet, CESNET-TLS22 and CESNET-QUIC22 (Luxemburk, ISP-scale), Stratosphere IPS malware captures (DeepMAL), 1300-DApp private set (GraphDApp), NetBench (2024 FM benchmark).
notes.recurring_models: Lineage: (1) raw-byte CNNs 2017-2018 (Wang 1D/2D-CNN, Deep Packet, Datanet); (2) sequence models on packet metadata (FS-Net bi-GRU, TSCRNN BiLSTM, DF CNN on directions); (3) image representations (FlowPic histograms, YaTC MFR matrices); (4) multimodal fusion (MIMETIC, SHAPE, MM4flow); (5) graphs (GraphDApp TIG, CGNN chained graph, TFE-GNN byte-PMI graphs, MH-Net multi-view units, FG-SAT flow graphs); (6) BERT-style byte-token pre-training (PERT -> ET-BERT -> TrafficFormer/FlowletFormer/TraGe/Nethira); (7) MAE-style (YaTC, ToN-MAE, NetMamba, FlowSem-MAE); (8) generative/LLM (NetGPT, TrafficGPT, Lens, TrafficLLM, MERLOT MoE); (9) SSM/efficiency (NetMamba, NetMamba+, MambaNetBurst); (10) foundation-model engineering (netFound hierarchical burst-flow attention, protocol-aware tokenization).
notes.input_representation_taxonomy: Five families determine what an explanation can even mean: raw bytes (token/byte saliency, e.g. Deep Packet, ET-BERT), packet-size/time/direction sequences (per-packet importance, e.g. FS-Net, Rosetta, DF), 2D images of flows (pixel saliency mapping to size-time bins or byte positions, e.g. FlowPic, YaTC), graphs (node/edge/subgraph importance, e.g. GraphDApp TIG, TFE-GNN byte graphs), flow-statistics/tabular (classic feature importance, e.g. CICFlowMeter features, FlowSem-MAE field units). nPrint is the special case engineered so every input bit maps to a named protocol header bit.
notes.author_stated_limitations: (1) Shortcut learning / benchmark artifacts: 'The Sweet Danger of Sugar' shows byte-level models exploit dataset artifacts (unencrypted header leftovers) on ISCXVPN2016-class benchmarks and that a header-only LM matches them - directly quoting the theme, models learn 'from headers, not from encrypted payload'; 'Bias in the Shadows' (2026) builds a model-agnostic shortcut-discovery framework; even Deep Packet (2017) masked MAC/IP fields to avoid identifying-field bias. (2) Robustness/distribution shift: Rosetta states existing DL models 'all have significant performance degradation in real diverse network environments' because TCP mechanisms alter packet-length sequences; follow-ups FG-SAT ('environment shifts'), UniAlign, PRIME ('declining plasticity'), drift-oriented self-evolving classification (2501.04246), PERO robust post-training. (3) Label scarcity motivates all pre-training papers: ET-BERT/TrafficFormer note labeling traffic 'requires expert knowledge of network protocols and specific attack scenarios'; Guarino et al. compare label-efficient regimes. (4) Closed-world assumption: open-world/OOD papers (Facing Unknown, TAO-Net, M3S-UPD, TrafficGPT-AINTEC, Luxemburk reject option) all state deployed classifiers meet unknown classes. (5) Representation-heterogeneity: TraGe/TrafficMoE/Nethira/FlowletFormer/SHAPE all argue uniform byte tokenization ignores header-vs-payload statistical differences and protocol-stack semantics. (6) Efficiency: NetMamba/MambaNetBurst/MERLOT/ECHO cite transformer quadratic cost and line-rate constraints; AutoML4ETC and HW-NAS treat architecture as the bottleneck. (7) Truncation bias: TrafficGPT notes token-length ceilings truncate flows (most byte models read only first k bytes/packets). (8) Reproducibility: IMC'23 Replication found dataset problems and inflated augmentation gains in a published flowpic result; 'One task to rule them all' finds weak cross-task/dataset generalizability; Demystifying NFM (NeurIPS'25) probes what FM latents encode and finds prior SOTA models fail exogenous-context tests (netFound reports others score below 0.62 F1 where it reaches 0.95). These author-stated gaps (shortcuts, fragility, opacity of pre-trained representations) are precisely the openings an XAI-for-traffic-classification thesis should exploit.
